entries.title: Exact complete-Cayley geometric-target Metropolis relaxation [draft; pending w347]
entries.statement: Let G have order n>=2 and identity e. For 0<alpha<=1 let P(x,x)=1-alpha and P(x,y)=alpha/(n-1) for y!=x. Start P at e and stop at independent T with P(T=k)=p(1-p)^k, k>=0, 0<p<1. Put b=1-alpha*n/(n-1) and a=p/(1-(1-p)*b). The Metropolis kernel M with proposal P and target Law(X_T) has spectral-gap relaxation time tau(M)=tau(P)*(1+(n-1)*a), where tau(P)=(n-1)/(alpha*n). It is strictly increasing in p. With alpha=p=1/2 both kernels are lazy and tau(M)/[n*tau(P)] tends to 2/3 as n tends to infinity. This family has proposal degree n-1 and does not settle a fixed-degree variant or a differently parametrised monotonicity question.
entries.proof_text: P acts as the scalar b on the space orthogonal to constants. Summing p*sum_k (1-p)^k P^k gives the displayed target. Every proposal from a nonidentity state is accepted. From e to any other state, its probability is alpha/(n-1) times r=(1-a)/(1+(n-1)*a). Thus the two-state radial lump has rates alpha*r and alpha/(n-1), and nonconstant eigenvalue 1-alpha*r-alpha/(n-1). The n-2 contrasts between nonidentity states have eigenvalue b. Since 0<a<1 and r<1, the radial eigenvalue is at least b and is lambda_2. Its gap is alpha*(r+1/(n-1))=alpha*n/((n-1)*(1+(n-1)*a)). Inversion proves the formula, including n=2 where the contrast subspace is empty. Differentiating a=p/(1-b+b*p) gives a prime=(1-b)/(1-b+b*p)^2>0. For alpha=p=1/2, a=(n-1)/(3*n/2-1), so (1+(n-1)*a)/n tends to 2/3.
assumptions: Geo0 convention and inverse ordinary spectral gap

relations.rationale: New card: "This family has proposal degree n-1"; existing card: "Control the relaxation time of Metropolis random walk targeting the distribution of a Cayley walk at an independent geometric time; in particular, test monotonic decrease in the geometric parameter". This result treats an explicitly stated special case or limitation; it does not certify a solution.
New card: "tau(M)=tau(P)*(1+(n-1)*a)"; existing card: "Monotone decrease is false already on the two-element Cayley group".
